_readme: Hand-written prose. The weekly build never touches this file. managers is keyed by site handle, seasons by year. Blank line between paragraphs.

managers.triccster:
Seventeen seasons, tied with Austin and Brett for the longest run in the league, and still nothing in the case. The regular season record is 111-103. The points are the more irritating number: 24,524 scored against 24,741 allowed across 253 games, a gap of under a point a game. Nobody here has been closer to exactly average for longer.

2020 was the year it should have happened, 12-3 and the best record he has ever put up. 2017 was the other end of it, 3-12, the only season the roster never got going at all.

2025 was the cruel one. He scored 1,898.7, more than any other team in the league, and finished third at 9-8. Anthony won the title with 113 fewer points.
managers.Colt45Johnson:
Thirteen seasons since 2013 and a regular season record of 88-86, which is about as level as a career gets. The title came early: 2014, 10-3 in the regular season and a 107.68 to 90.12 win over T.J. in the final. He was back in the final in 2017 and lost it to James.

His best team never got there. 2018 went 11-2 with 1,691.5 points, the most in the league that year, and lost the semifinal to Austin 133.26 to 92.22. Two seasons later he put up 201.0 in week 3 against Scott, the second-highest score in league history.

He also owns the lowest: 32.58 in week 10 of 2015. The last three years have been harder going, with 3-11 finishes in 2023 and 2025. He is 12-7 against Scott and 12-8 against T.J., and the group chat hears about both.
managers.Jbird531:
Twelve seasons, 100-61 in the regular season, and the best winning percentage of anyone still in the league. It did not start that way: 6-7 and 4-9 in his first two years.

Two titles, 2020 and 2022, and both finals were against T.J., 123.46 to 119.70 and then 95.32 to 75.20. He leads that series 12-4.

The ones that got away were bigger. 2019 went 12-1, the best regular season record in league history, and ended in a 163.68 to 147.38 semifinal loss to T.J. 2024 went 11-3 as the top seed and ran into Brett's 172.78 in the semifinal.
managers.PapaMidnight:
Nine seasons since 2017, a 43-79 regular season record, and one playoff trip. It was a good one while it lasted: 2019, 6-7 as the sixth seed, a 132.36 to 87.30 quarterfinal win over Zach Nase, then a 121.22 to 69.58 loss to James, who went on to win the title.

The low points repeat. Three separate seasons ended 3-10 or 3-11. The high point was 175.22 in week 5 of 2021, the best score anyone put up that season.

Two series say the most about him. He is 12-6 against Zach Nase, his best record against anyone, and 3-11 against Zak. 2025 finished 7-7, tied for the best record he has had.
managers.RockMNwild:
Four titles, the most in league history: 2012, 2016, 2018 and 2021. Sixteen seasons back to 2008, a 115-99 regular season, and a 14-7 playoff record that no other current manager is close to.

Two of those titles came against Zak in the final, 143.96 to 123.08 in 2018 and 93.16 to 89.72 in 2021. He rarely needs the top seed to do it; 2018 was won from fourth and 2021 from fourth again. He reached the final last season too and lost it to Anthony, 144.14 to 81.62.

The one manager he has not solved is T.J., who leads the series 15-8. The site has seventeen team names on file for him, and that only counts the ones that lasted long enough to be recorded.
managers.TuanonStan:
James holds the highest score in league history, 224.06 in week 5 of 2019 against Brett. Three weeks later he put up 183.16. He won the title that year too, beating T.J. 147.76 to 119.12 in the final.

That was his second. The first came in 2017: 11-2, the most points in the league, a 126.58 to 84.74 semifinal over Zak and a 108.12 to 90.24 final over Colt. The year before he had also gone 11-2 and lost the final to Austin.

Fourteen seasons, 104-83. 2013 finished 2-11, the worst record in the league that year. He is 10-2 against Scott and 10-15 against Austin, the one long series that has never gone his way.
managers.Wallner:
Thirteen seasons since 2013, 83-91, five playoff trips and no title yet. He arrived with the most points in the league, 1,423.8 in 2013, and made the playoffs at 7-6.

The closest he has come was 2021. Dos Gesickis went 11-3 and took the top seed, then lost the semifinal to Zak 140.80 to 100.48. His lowest week came in 2024, 37.46 in week 2.

He is 9-7 against Colt, 8-5 against Brett and 8-13 against James. He also gave a kicker, Chad Ryland, the nickname RKO Legend Killer, which in this league is about the highest honor a kicker can get.
managers.YoungBuck04:
The commissioner, with four finals and one title. He lost to Austin in 2018 and 2021, and to Brett in 2024, 127.68 to 121.22.

The win, in 2023, came the hard way. Zak went 7-7, took the sixth seed, and then beat Joey by 2.04, James by 46.46 and Scott 145.40 to 124.24. A year later he went 10-4, led the league with 1,708.5 points, and lost the final.

Fourteen seasons, 100-87. Some of his series are among the most one-sided in the league: 11-3 against Mikey and 11-4 against Zach Nase. SKOL.
managers.brettmn13:
Two titles, eleven years apart, both from the sixth seed. 2013 was won at 7-6. 2024 was won at 7-7, and on the way he put up 172.78 against Joey in the semifinal, the highest score anyone has posted in a playoff game here, before beating Zak 127.68 to 121.22.

Sixteen seasons, 111-103, and eleven playoff trips, tied with Austin for the most. In between the titles there were some rough ones: 3-10 in 2015 and again in 2019.

He also hosts the draft, cooks for it, and has campaigned to get rid of the kicker. The vote went against him, and the 2026 roster still has a K slot.
managers.butterygoop:
The reigning champion. Anthony's title came in his eighth season, 2025, and the final was not close: 144.14 to 81.62 over Austin.

He arrived in 2018 and made the playoffs straight away at 9-4. It has been uneven since, 3-10 in 2020 and 5-9 in 2024, with playoff seasons in 2021 and 2022 in between. The career regular season sits at 53-56 through last year.

His best single week is 171.68, in week 2 of 2022 against Joey. He is 9-4 against Zach Nase and 3-8 against Austin, his one real problem.
managers.snelson91:
Scott won the 2015 title in the lowest-scoring final the league has played since 2014: 64.70 to 60.08 over Tyler. He had gone 8-5 and beat Austin 103.66 to 82.48 in the semifinal.

He got back to a final in 2023 at 8-6, with the eleventh-most points in the league, and lost it to Zak. Twelve seasons, 72-89, four playoff trips, and a 5-3 record once he is in.

His best day was 180.2 in week 6 of 2018, against T.J., the highest score of that season. The two series that have gone worst are Zak, 8-17, and James, 2-10.
managers.thecreamer:
Twelve seasons since 2014, 69-92, and two playoff trips: 2016 at 6-7, and 2019, when he went 9-4 and finished third in the regular season. Both ended in the first game, and neither was close: 146.04 to 61.88 against Austin in 2016, 132.36 to 87.30 against Mikey in 2019.

The two highest scores of 2023 were both his, 164.66 in week 3 and 159.18 in week 5. The lowest of 2025 was his too, 42.9 in week 11.

The team has been called thecreamer since 2021, one of two in the league that has not been renamed since then. He is 9-7 against Brett and 5-13 against Austin.

seasons.2025:
Anthony's first title, in his eighth season. He went 10-6 and finished third in scoring, which two better-scoring teams will be thinking about for a while.

T.J. led the league with 1,898.7 points and finished third at 9-8. James put up the second most, 1,827.7, and went 8-9. Scoring was not the problem for either of them.

Week 11 produced both floors of the season on the same Sunday: Zach Nase 42.9 and Colt 53.2. The high was Scott's 158.0 in week 8, and it came against the team that went on to win it all.
seasons.2008:
The first season on record: eight teams on Yahoo, standard scoring, whole-number points. DJ won it. He went 9-5, beat T.J. 121 to 81 in the semifinal and the Broncos 100 to 77 in the final.

Brett, DJ and T.J. all finished 9-5. The Broncos had the most points, 1,295, and reached the final from the fourth seed. The best single score of the year, 150 in week 12, belonged to a team called kicked out next year, which went 3-11.
seasons.2010:
2009 is not in the archive, so the record picks up here, with twelve teams and a six-team playoff. The Broncos won it, 87 to 68 over DJ in the final, after beating T.J. 76 to 65 in the semifinal.

Brett had the best season on paper, 10-3 with the most points, and lost his first playoff game to T.J., 98 to 45. T.J. had the tenth-most points in the league and reached the semifinal anyway. He also had the best single week, 148 in week 3.
seasons.2012:
Austin's first title. He went 10-3, beat James 101 to 66 in the semifinal and Tyler 107 to 88 in the final. 2011 is missing from the archive, like 2009.

Brett took third, and his 157 in the third-place game was the highest score of the season. T.J. finished 5-7 and missed the playoffs.
seasons.2013:
Brett's first title, won from the sixth seed at 7-6. He beat the team listed as 2012 champ 142.52 to 124.02, T.J. 130.32 to 100.16 and Tyler 107.44 to 70.84. It was Tyler's second straight loss in a final.

Tyler had the best record at 10-3. John Wallner scored the most, 1,423.8, in his first season. James went 2-11. This was the last year of standard scoring, so point totals from here back do not compare with what came after.
seasons.2014:
Colt's title, in his second season. He went 10-3, beat Tyler 80.48 to 66.70 in the semifinal and T.J. 107.68 to 90.12 in the final. T.J. had come through from the sixth seed, beating Brett and J Rock on the way.

Zak scored the most points, 1,349.8, and went 7-6. Joey, Scott and Zach Nase all played their first seasons. Austin had the lowest score of the year, 41.22 in week 6.
seasons.2015:
Scott's title, in the lowest-scoring final the league has played since 2014: 64.70 to 60.08 over Tyler. Tyler had gone 9-4 with the most points and put up 155.40 in the semifinal a week earlier.

Colt scored 32.58 in week 10, which is still the lowest score in league history. Brett went 3-10.
seasons.2016:
Austin's second title, from the third seed at 8-5. He opened the playoffs with 146.04 against Zach Nase, the highest score of the year, then beat Zak 106.46 to 92.18 and James 129.76 to 111.58.

James had gone 11-2 with the most points in the league and lost the final. Zach Nase made his first playoff appearance. J Rock finished 3-10.
seasons.2017:
James went 11-2 again and this time finished it: the most points in the league, 1,430.7, a 126.58 to 84.74 semifinal over Zak and a 108.12 to 90.24 final over Colt.

T.J. finished last at 3-10 with the fewest points, 955.6. Mikey's first season also ended 3-10.
seasons.2018:
Austin's third title, from the fourth seed. He beat Joey 151.88 to 75.40, Colt 133.26 to 92.22 and Zak 143.96 to 123.08.

Colt had the best season, 11-2 with 1,691.5 points, and went out in the semifinal. Anthony joined and went 9-4. Scott put up 180.2 in week 6, against T.J., the best single score of the year. Zach Nase went 2-11.
seasons.2019:
James's second title, and the season of the highest score in league history: his 224.06 in week 5 against Brett. He beat Mikey 121.22 to 69.58 in the semifinal and T.J. 147.76 to 119.12 in the final.

Joey went 12-1, the best regular season record the league has seen, and lost the semifinal to T.J., 163.68 to 147.38. It was Mikey's only playoff appearance to date. Brett and Colt both went 3-10.
seasons.2020:
Joey's first title, 123.46 to 119.70 over T.J., a margin of 3.76. T.J. had gone 11-2 and taken the top seed, the best regular season of his career.

Colt scored the most, 1,580.5, and put up 201.0 in week 3, the second-highest score in league history. It was the last season on Yahoo. Anthony went 3-10.
seasons.2021:
The first season on Sleeper, and Austin's fourth title, from the fourth seed at 8-6: 143.96 to 88.64 over Anthony in the semifinal and 93.16 to 89.72 over Zak in the final.

John Wallner had the best record, 11-3, and lost the semifinal to Zak. Joey scored the most points, 1,646.7. Mikey had the best single week, 175.22 in week 5.
seasons.2022:
Joey's second title, and his second final win over T.J., 95.32 to 75.20. Joey went 12-2 with the most points in the league. T.J. came from the sixth seed and beat Anthony and Colt to get there.

Anthony put up the high score of the season, 171.68 in week 2. Austin went 4-10, a year after winning it.
seasons.2023:
Zak's title, won from the sixth seed at 7-7. He beat Joey by 2.04 in the quarterfinal, James 137.28 to 90.82 and Scott 145.40 to 124.24. Scott reached the final at 8-6 with the eleventh-most points in the league.

James went 10-4 with the most points and did not get past the semifinal. Zach Nase had the season's two highest scores. Colt went 3-11.
seasons.2024:
Brett's second title, and the second year running that the sixth seed won it. He beat Austin 97.04 to 83.74, then Joey with 172.78, the highest score ever posted in a playoff game here, and Zak 127.68 to 121.22 in the final.

Zak had gone 10-4 with the most points in the league, 1,708.5, and lost the final a year after winning it. Joey had the best record at 11-3. John Wallner's 37.46 in week 2 was the season low.
